description: The chart represents the distribution of four categories (N+K+, N-K+, N-K-, and N+K-) across three difficulty levels (easy, medium, and hard) in a zero-shot context. Each pie chart has four slices, corresponding to the four categories, and is labeled with the respective difficulty level. The slices are colored according to a legend on the right, with N+K+ in teal, N-K+ in beige, N-K- in brown, and N+K- in red. For the "easy" chart, the proportions are approximately 55.4% (N+K+, teal), 38.3% (N-K+, beige), 4.6% (N-K-, brown), and 1.7% (N+K-, red); for "medium", they are 58.8% (N+K+, teal), 35.4% (N-K+, beige), 4.0% (N-K-, brown), and 1.8% (N+K-, red); and for "hard", they are 37.3% (N+K+, teal), 37.9% (N-K-, brown), 18.1% (N-K+, beige), and 6.7% (N+K-, red). The percentage labels are shown inside each slice. The charts do not visually emphasize any particular slice. The proportions of the slices vary across the three difficulty levels, with the "hard" chart showing a more even distribution among the categories compared to "easy" and "medium".
